Subject: Data residency & region pinning - quick follow-up

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful overview. I wanted to capture the outstanding questions we have on our side so we can move toward a technical deep dive and procurement. Attaching our initial requirements PDF (FirstTrust-Initial-Requirements.pdf).

Top questions we need clarified before sharing with IT/security: 
1) Region pinning: can we pin a workload to a single region (US-East) for data-at-rest and inference execution? If so, how strict is the pin (e.g., are metadata/control-plane signals allowed to cross regions)?
2) Cross-region failover: what is the failover behavior if a region goes down? Is there synchronous replication or async replication? What RPO/RTO should we expect?
3) Backups & retention: frequency of snapshots, retention windows (30/90/365 days) and ability to control retention per-environment (prod vs staging).
4) Backup encryption & KMS: do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) for backups? Are backups stored in same region as the workload by default?
5) Request/response logging & PII: are request/response payloads logged by default? Can we opt-out or truncate/hide PII? Are there redaction features or middleware hooks?
6) Deletion / GDPR right-to-be-forgotten: how promptly can data tied to a customer be removed (snapshots, cache, logs)?

Next steps we'd like: a short written response to the items above, then a tech deep-dive with your platform/security leads, and a rough procurement timeline so we can coordinate our internal PMs.

Thanks,
Jamie Torres

Jamie — thanks for this and for the time today. Appreciate the clear list. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps; I'm looping in Stephanie from Security to provide the detailed answers and the architecture diagram. Rachel (CS) will own the scheduling and procurement intro.

Recap / quick answers (high level):
- Region pinning: Supported. You can pin workloads to a single region for inference and storage. Control-plane metadata may occasionally route via our primary control plane in the same geo region; we can provide a Private deployment option if you need absolute control.
- Cross-region failover: Supported via replicating model states and snapshots. We typically run async replication for cross-region to avoid synchronous write latencies; we can discuss RPO/RTO tradeoffs during the deep dive.
- Backups: Snapshots can be taken hourly/daily with configurable retention windows. Default is 30 days for logs, 90 days for snapshots on hosted tier; Dedicated/Private allow longer retention.
- KMS/CMK: We support customer-managed keys for Private deployments, and we have integration options for enterprise KMS for Dedicated.
- Logging / PII: Request/response logging is configurable. By default we store minimal request metadata and token-level usage; storing full request/response is opt-in. Stephanie will detail redaction and retention controls.
- Deletion: We support data deletion APIs and documented deletion workflows; timing depends on retention policy and snapshot schedules.

Proposed next steps:
1) Stephanie to send technical detail + architecture diagram and SOC2 summary (cc'd).
2) Schedule 60-min tech deep dive (platform + security) — Rachel will propose times.
3) Procurement intro and a first-pass term sheet (we can provide a template).

We can also provide a short replication matrix (RPO/RTO by replication mode) ahead of the call.

Hi Jamie — thanks for the list. Below are the detailed answers to each item and some implementation notes. Attaching our SOC2 summary and a region architecture diagram (redwood-region-arch.png).

1) Region pinning
- Supported across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. For Hosted customers we offer per-customer routing policies that pin inference execution and persistent storage to a chosen region (US, EU, APAC).
- Control-plane calls (account management/metrics) may touch our control plane endpoints; we can restrict control plane traffic to the same region for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- For the strictest residency (no cross-region metadata), we recommend Private deployment (VPC) with a local control plane.

2) Cross-region failover
- We support active-standby and async-replication topologies. By default cross-region replication is asynchronous (to avoid synchronous write latency impact). Typical RPOs for async replication are in the 5–30 minute range depending on throughput; RTOs depend on model size and cache warming (~5–30 minutes for model reload + KV cache warm).
- For lower RPOs we can configure synchronous replication within a single cloud region’s availability zones or set up regional clusters with more frequent snapshotting — this is a tradeoff between cost, latency, and complexity.

3) Backups & retention
- Snapshots: configurable cadence (hourly/daily) and retention policy per environment. Hosted defaults: 90-day snapshot retention for production; 30-day for non-prod. Dedicated/Private can be configured up to 365+ days with different SLAs.
- Backups are stored in the selected region by default; cross-region copies are optional and explicit.

4) Backup encryption & KMS
- All snapshots and persistent storage are encrypted at rest. We support provider-managed keys and customer-managed keys (CMK) for Dedicated/Private deployments. CMK options include AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault where applicable.

5) Request/response logging & PII
- Default: we store minimal request metadata (timestamp, model, token usage, request id). Full request/response bodies are NOT stored by default for hosted customers unless explicitly enabled.
- You can opt-in to full logging for debugging and then schedule automatic truncation or redaction of sensitive fields. We provide a redaction middleware you can deploy client-side or configure server-side to replace PII before logs are persisted (email, SSN, account numbers).
- For the highest assurance, we offer a “no request body logging” mode and recommend using client-side tokenization or field-level hashing before sending sensitive attributes.

6) Deletion / GDPR right-to-be-forgotten
- We provide documented deletion APIs to remove customer data from active stores. For snapshots and backups, deletion is subject to the snapshot retention window unless you request immediate purge (we support expedited deletion for compliance requests under a contractual SLA).
- We maintain an audit trail of deletion requests (who requested, when).

Other notes
- Logs retention: request metadata default 30 days; you can extend to 90/365 or push logs to your own log sink (recommended for long-term audit).
- Backups & cross-region copies incur storage and egress costs — we document cost impacts per configuration.
